page: Microsoft Azure M176bds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. Built on the x86_64 architecture and provisioned via Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz. It supplies 88 physical cores and 176 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled, accompanied by 105 MB of L3 cache. The memory configuration totals 1,536 GB of RAM, offering approximately 8.73 GB of memory per core. Bundled storage includes a 429 GB local SSD with Premium Storage support, while no dedicated GPUs are integrated into the host.

Benchmark measurements indicate high multi-threaded throughput alongside moderate single-thread execution speeds. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves a multi-core score of 141,482.89, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances, against an average single-core rating of 2,055.29. Memory bandwidth reaches 432.14 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 11,579.05 GB/sec for cached blocks. The architecture demonstrates strong key-value and database handling, generating 170.86 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and a top-tier score of 34,532.09 in PassMark database tests. Built-in vector and matrix flags, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, support CPU-based inference workloads.

The primary operational tradeoff lies in local disk density; the 429 GB local SSD serves temporary needs but requires supplemental remote storage for persistent or high-capacity data tiers. Additionally, complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not provided. The M176bds_v3 provides efficient resource consolidation for large-footprint in-memory databases, enterprise caching systems, high-concurrency web backends, and multi-threaded analytical pipelines requiring substantial RAM-per-thread ratios.
